stem: Which clinical feature distinguishes the rash of meningococcal disease from many other common childhood viral exanthems?

options.text: It typically starts on the head and moves to the feet.
It is a non-blanching petechial or purpuric rash.
It produces a 'honey-colored' crust when the vesicles burst.
It appears as a 'slapped cheek' followed by a lacy pattern.

explanation: The inability of the rash to disappear under pressure (non-blanching) is a critical warning sign of invasive meningococcal disease.
rationale: Think about what happens to the color of the rash when you apply pressure with a glass.

optionExplanations.A: This downward progression is more characteristic of the measles rash.
optionExplanations.B: The inability of the rash to disappear under pressure (non-blanching) is a critical warning sign of invasive meningococcal disease.
optionExplanations.C: Honey-colored crusting is the hallmark of impetigo, not meningococcal disease.
optionExplanations.D: This pattern is the classic presentation of Fifth Disease.
